text: Consider the case of the Misses Penrose, whose mother, a woman of unwavering determination, had resolved to see them both advantageously married before the close of the season. Her methods, however, were somewhat… unorthodox. Rather than allowing her daughters the freedom to cultivate genuine attachments, she actively discouraged any acquaintance that did not promise a substantial financial return. “Sensibility,” she declared, with a dismissive wave of her hand, “is all very well, but it will not put bread on the table.” The consequence was a series of strained conversations and awkward encounters, as the Misses Penrose attempted to feign interest in gentlemen they actively disliked, all under the watchful eye of their formidable mother. It was a spectacle, one could not help but think, more akin to a commercial transaction than a courtship.
